title: Personal Checking: Combined Deposit Balance Measured at Close of Business on the Cycle Closing Date
content:
## Purpose

Personal Checking defines a combined deposit balance of its own for one determination: the same-day review of a monthly maintenance fee that is dated the cycle closing date while that date is still the current business day, in which the tier's waiver for combined holdings is decided. This page defines that balance — the moment it describes, what it takes in, and how its parts are made up.

## When the balance is read

The balance describes the account at close of business on the cycle closing date. It takes in every posting made to the account in the course of that business day, and every credit the bank already owes the account; the one posting it does not take in is the refund of the maintenance fee whose review it serves. Any entry becomes part of a ledger balance at the moment it posts, and not sooner: a credit that is merely pending is no part of it.

## Credits the bank already owes

For this balance, a credit the bank already owes the account is either of the following:

- a refund of any fee that is due on the bank-error ground, or due because a dispute has been resolved in the owner's favour — whatever the fee is, and whichever Personal Checking rule decides that the refund is due;
- a provisional credit that has fallen due on a dispute still in submitted status, whichever rule fixes its amount.

The refund that this very review may produce is excluded from them. Nor is a courtesy refund ever owed: it is goodwill, which the bank grants only when the customer asks for it.

## What goes into it

The balance is the total of the following parts:

| Part | What is taken |
|---|---|
| This checking account | whatever its posted ledger shows, with an overdrawn figure entering as zero |
| Savings | for each of the statuses applied, active and dormant, what the owner's savings account in that status currently holds — one account per status |
| Certificates | the principal of the owner's certificate of deposit in applied status, in active status and in grace period status — one certificate for each of those statuses |
| Mortgage | only where this checking account's tier counts mortgage principal: the principal of the owner's mortgage loan in active, delinquent and forbearance status, one loan for each; on any other tier, nothing |

Two exclusions apply. The owner's other checking accounts are not counted at all. Where the owner holds more than one savings account, certificate or mortgage loan in the same status, only the first one on the customer's record is counted.

Balances on the Savings & Money Market Accounts, Certificates of Deposit and Home Mortgage Loans records are read as they stand on that date.

## Worked total (hypothetical holdings, tier not counting mortgage principal)

- This checking account at close of business: 1850.00 USD.
- Savings: one active account at 2400.00 USD and one dormant account at 300.00 USD.
- Certificates: one active certificate with 5000.00 USD principal, and one closed certificate.
- A second checking account of the owner at 4000.00 USD, and a mortgage loan.

Total: 1850.00 plus 2400.00 plus 300.00 plus 5000.00, which is 9550.00 USD. The closed certificate, the second checking account and, on this tier, the mortgage add nothing. Had this checking account closed the day overdrawn, its part would be zero and the total 7700.00 USD.
